prompt: In many growing cities, most new homes are now built as flats in high-rise tower blocks rather than as individual houses with gardens. Do the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
As cities absorb more people, a growing proportion of new homes are being built as flats in tower blocks rather than as houses with gardens. I believe the advantages of this trend outweigh the disadvantages, although the balance depends heavily on who the buildings are designed for.

The strongest argument for building upwards concerns land. A city that grows outwards consumes farmland and open countryside, and it also commits its residents to long commutes, because jobs and services cannot follow a population spread thinly across a wide area. Density reverses this. When several hundred households live on one site, a frequent bus route, a school and a row of shops become viable within walking distance, and the cost of supplying water and electricity to each home falls. In that sense a tower block is not only a way of housing people but of making local services affordable.

The drawbacks are real, but they are unevenly distributed. For young professionals and older couples, a well-managed flat is often preferable to a house: it is easier to maintain, more secure and closer to work. Families with small children are in a different position. Without a garden or a safe courtyard, play has to be supervised and planned, and parents on the fifteenth floor cannot simply send a child outside. Tower blocks also depend on shared systems such as lifts, fire doors and communal heating, and when these are neglected the residents have little ability to repair them themselves.

Overall, I think building upwards is the more sensible direction for a crowded city, provided it is not treated as a single solution for everyone. Planners should combine tall blocks for smaller households with lower-rise family housing nearby, so that density is achieved without asking parents to raise children in the sky.
title: High-rise flats instead of family houses
